$$
x=4u+a,\,y=6u+bv+c
$$

[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4u \\ 6u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4u \\ 6u+2v-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
x=4u+0,\,y=6u+2v+(-1)
$$

$$
a+b+c=0+2+(-1)=1.

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix. 

Under this notation, 

- $[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]$ represents vectors belonging to the input space, and

- $[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]$  represents vectors belonging to the output space.

For example,

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]
$$

is an affine transformation because it can be expressed in the form $\mathbf x = A\mathbf u + \mathbf b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+1 \\ 2u+v-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

However, the transformation

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]
$$

is not affine since it contains the quadratic term $uv.$

Finally, note the following relationships between affine and linear transformations:

- A linear transformation $\mathbf x = A \mathbf u$ is a special case of an affine transformation with $\mathbf b = \mathbf 0.$

$$

However, the transformation

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]
